heading: Networks can fit permuted pixels and Gaussian noise to zero training error
definition: the same networks also fit shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs to zero training error.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce fitting on permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs in MLPs and CNNs. The demonstrated settings retain qualifications about training budget and model capacity.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 for tested models with parameter size not stated. The counts do not permit separate levels for toy, <1B, 1–10B, 10–100B or >100B settings.
suggested_status.reason: Non-original results reproduce fitting across the input branches in MLP/CNN experiments, including arXiv:2106.04181#R9, arXiv:2106.04181#R12 and arXiv:2106.04181#R14. Gaussian fitting also appears in VGG-11 (arXiv:1805.07291#R33) and modified ResNet-50 (10.1101/2022.03.31.486580#R1). counts: versions.V3.verdicts.supports.studies=17; versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original=1; versions.V3.studies_with_limits_scope=5; versions.V3.studies_with_challenges=0. versions.V3.studies_by_size contains only 'not stated'. The proposed level applies to the demonstrated settings, with the budget and capacity qualifications retained.
suggested_status.open_questions: Matched-budget tests of the original Inception configuration would clarify the incomplete-fitting comparison. Documented parameter counts and matched full-dataset tests across all input transformations would establish scale and capacity boundaries. Missing endpoint rows should be extracted before source-level verification.

source.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; B. Recht; O. Vinyals

original_result.setup: Zhang et al. trained Inception on CIFAR10 with shuffled pixels, random-valued pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
original_result.result: The study showed training-loss curves for all three input types, without numerical values.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Modified ResNet-50 perfectly fitted Gaussian random-pixel images with random initialization or ImageNet pretraining.
Networks reached perfect training accuracy on Gaussian-noise inputs in the MNIST experiments.
Overcomplete ReLU networks achieved zero training error on Gaussian inputs with nearly random targets.
VGG-11 perfectly fitted Gaussian-noise inputs with each tested training configuration.
Networks provably fit shuffled or noise inputs given sufficient width and normalized, sufficiently separated inputs.
Networks memorized Gaussian inputs with random ten-class labels.
ResNet-34 nearly perfectly fitted datasets where 40% of inputs were Gaussian noise or had shuffled pixels.
Depth-two networks provably achieved zero training classification error on Gaussian inputs with independent random labels.
MLP, CNN, and GRU models perfectly fitted MNIST-1D after shuffling features identically in every input.
ResNet-34 nearly perfectly fitted CIFAR10 where 40% of inputs were Gaussian noise or had shuffled pixels.
Binary MNIST and CIFAR10 networks perfectly fitted permuted, Gaussian, and white-noise inputs.
ResNet-50 fitted entirely Gaussian ImageNet inputs and mixtures of real and Gaussian images.
Sufficiently wide networks achieved zero loss on Gaussian inputs and targets.
MLPs and CNNs perfectly fitted Gaussian or identically shuffled inputs, within measured limits on dataset size.
ReLU networks perfectly fitted Gaussian inputs with independent random labels at both tested dataset sizes.
A CNN fully memorized random-pixel inputs with fixed training settings.
ResNet-20 perfectly fitted CIFAR-10 augmented with randomly labeled Gaussian images.
Strong noise in unit activations reduced the Small-inception network's random-pixel training accuracy to chance.
Inception reached only 50.0% training accuracy after 200 epochs with each image's pixels shuffled differently.
Shuffling pixel positions reduced how many samples CNNs could fit perfectly, compared with unshuffled inputs.
ReLU networks failed to perfectly fit Gaussian datasets larger than they could memorize.
One training policy failed to fully memorize random-pixel inputs within 100 epochs.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Empirical fitting of entirely independently permuted ImageNet inputs by practical image-classification networks.
untested.basis: The original's untested-parts line reports no ImageNet randomized-input experiment. arXiv:2203.10036#R2 covers Gaussian ImageNet inputs and explicitly leaves permutations untested. arXiv:2406.11463#R6 measures shared-permutation capacity on ImageNet-20MS. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.training and versions.V3.main_rows_by_operation do not distinguish input transformations; the full pack supplies no independent-permutation ImageNet endpoint.

untested.what: Final zero training error after continual learning across shared-permutation MNIST tasks.
untested.basis: arXiv:2505.09486#R5 and arXiv:2505.09486#R6 measure average online accuracy during one-epoch tasks; their verdict fixes and untested-parts line leave final fitting undetermined. Other fitting results in the pack concern different training settings. counts: versions.V3.rows_by_state.cannot_determine and versions.V3.studies_by_stage do not establish a continual-learning endpoint.

wording_issues.issue: The original randomized-input learning curves specifically identify a small Inception model on CIFAR10: one shared pixel permutation across training and test images, a different permutation independently applied to each image, or Gaussian pixels matching the original dataset's mean and variance. The introduction reports zero training error on random-noise inputs. These results cannot be assigned to every architecture used elsewhere in that paper. Mathematical fitting guarantees also depend on specialized architecture, initialization or input assumptions rather than establishing unchanged structured-data training settings.

The ResNet-34 mixed-corruption reports state nearly perfect accuracy. The entirely Gaussian ImageNet ResNet-50 report distinguishes zero loss from near-perfect accuracy. The Gaussian-input memorization statement in arXiv:1905.11515 provides no numerical training-error endpoint or architecture identification.

wording_issues.phrase: shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs
wording_issues.issue: For the small Inception model on CIFAR10, one shared pixel permutation is applied across training and test images in the shared-permutation condition; a different permutation is applied independently to each image in the independent-permutation condition. Keep shared permutations, fixed independent per-image permutations and freshly sampled arrays distinct. The random-pixel arrays in arXiv:2610.16090 have no specified distribution; the white-noise replacements in arXiv:2106.04181 are not specified as Gaussian.

Fitting depends on training policy, dataset size and effective capacity: fraction-scaled random-pixel runs can remain incomplete, CNN permutation reduces perfectly fitted sample capacity, and Gaussian-input teachers fail at sufficiently high sample complexity.

method_sensitivity.what: The random-pixel CNN achieves complete memorization under the fixed policy but fails within 100 epochs under the fraction-scaled policy at fractions 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0.
A shared permutation leaves MLP fitting capacity unchanged but reduces CNN capacity. Gaussian replacement increases capacity for both architectures.

For small-inception on Gaussian random-pixel images, training accuracy progressively declines with increasing activation noise and reaches chance at sufficiently strong noise after 100 epochs. Intermediate noise conditions show declining accuracy; the chance-level endpoint applies only to sufficiently strong noise. The report varies activation function and bottleneck alongside noise; it does not supply an exact threshold in the linked row.

In the Gaussian-input, Gaussian-target ReLU experiment, loss after convergence transitions from 1 to 0 across width settings as layer widths reach order sqrt(N). These are endpoints across widths, not initial and final losses over training; exact coordinates and a numerical transition threshold remain figure-only. Fixed ReLU teachers perfectly fit the Figure 5 datasets but fit imperfectly in Figure 6's high-sample-complexity regimes; those teacher endpoints lack extracted rows.

On ImageNet mixed with Gaussian replacements, ordinary-SGD aggregation A3 learns both pristine and corrupt examples, while the M3 comparator learns pristine examples without learning the Gaussian subset.
